question: The network team needs permissions to access the Cisco UCS B-Series Servers via the Cisco UCS Manager GUI to configure the network and collect information about faults. The administrator wants to assign these permissions to the newly configured user called netops. Which set of tasks must the administrator perform to accomplish these goals?
options:
Implement username netops on the locally authenticated user.
Assign the roles of network administrator and operations.

Configure username netops on the Cisco UCS Manager login profile.
Assign the roles of AAA administrator and operations.

Enable username netops on the authenticated users.
Assign the roles of storage administrator and facility manager.

Deploy username netops on the users locales.
Assign the roles of networks security and facility manager.
theory: The netops user's needs (configure network settings, view faults) map directly to two Cisco UCS Manager built-in roles: Network Administrator (read/write to fabric interconnect infrastructure and network security operations) and Operations (read/write to system logs and faults). Since the user only needs standard UCS Manager GUI login (not remote AAA or locale-scoped multi-tenant access), the account should be created as a locally authenticated user with both roles assigned. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 19 - Securing UCS Management, Local Accounts and Roles)
